answer: Admission by reproducible analysis: each applicant draws one unassigned slice of the public Lotus benchmark from the orchard of 10,000 slices and publishes a signed quill report — a notebook re-deriving that slice’s published result from raw data, with code, data hashes, and each number shown. Two random verifiers re-run it; both reproductions must match within tolerance or the identity fails and the slice retires. A farm needs 3,000 analyst hours for 1,000 puppets — 3 hours per unique slice, no reuse, no bulk shortcut — while one honest applicant spends one 3-hour afternoon.
